document_name: GBV News AI GCS Storage Context
purpose: Machine-readable context for Codex/AI agents implementing Google Cloud Storage persistence for gbv-news-ai.
scope: Actual GCS buckets already created plus required object layout, permissions, naming, and linkage to Supabase PostgreSQL.

note: The following three Google Cloud Storage buckets have already been created and should be treated as the active durable storage targets.

purpose: Durable storage of original fetched article/source HTML before parsing.
Durable storage of normalized/versioned article JSON produced by parser code.
Durable storage of collection-run progress, reports, logs, and Wayback/CDX cache artifacts.

decision: All real collected research data and run artifacts go to GCS. Local filesystem paths must not be the authoritative storage or resume mechanism.
flow: write raw source object to gs://gbv-news-ai-raw
write processed JSON object to gs://gbv-news-ai-processed
record metadata and object URIs in Supabase PostgreSQL

rule: GCS uses object-name prefixes rather than real filesystem folders.
implementation: The application creates the apparent subfolder hierarchy automatically by uploading objects whose names contain '/'. No prior folder creation is required.
example: Uploading object name nation/2026/08/<article_id>/<raw_content_hash>.html automatically appears under nation/2026/08/ in the Cloud Console.

note: Content-addressed names preserve distinct immutable captures without overwriting an earlier response.
Parser version and normalized content hash prevent new extraction versions from overwriting older research outputs.
Trial and monthly runs use the same durable run-artifact architecture.

database_relationship: collection_runs stores run identity/configuration/status; detailed progress/report/cache artifacts remain in GCS and are addressed by run_name.

rule: Capture the returned GCS object generation identifier when writing raw and processed objects so exact object versions can be tracked.
Raw GCS persistence must succeed before processing is considered durable.

requirements: Do not silently overwrite existing raw objects.
Prefer create-if-absent/generation preconditions for raw object writes.
Processed outputs are versioned by parser_version in the object path.
Retries must reuse existing logical articles and identical article_versions rather than create duplicates.
A database failure after GCS upload must not require refetching the article; indexing should be safely retryable.

requirement: The application/service account must be able to create and read objects in all three buckets.
folder_permission_note: No special create-folder permission is needed because folders are object-name prefixes.
principle: Use bucket/object-level least privilege; the app should not require permission to create/delete buckets or change IAM.

production: Use the App Engine service identity / Application Default Credentials to authenticate to GCS.
local_development: Use gcloud auth application-default login for developer access where appropriate.
prohibited: Do not commit service-account JSON keys or embed GCP credentials in source code.

note: Bucket names are configuration, not secrets.

current_repository_state: Existing collector currently writes raw HTML, processed JSON, run progress, CSV reports, logs, lock files, and CDX caches beneath local data/trials paths.
target_state: Production/real trial/monthly collection should no longer use those local paths as durable storage. GCS becomes authoritative; Supabase becomes the structured tracking/index layer.

criteria: A trial run can execute without creating durable collected files under data/trials/.
Raw article source is visible in gbv-news-ai-raw under source/year/month prefix.
Processed JSON is visible in gbv-news-ai-processed under parser_version/source/year/month prefix.
Run progress/report/cache artifacts are stored in gbv-news-ai-runs under run_name.
Supabase article_versions contains matching gs:// URIs and GCS generation values where available.
App code creates prefix/subfolder structures automatically through object names.
Reruns are idempotent and do not silently overwrite raw source evidence.
